items.stem: What is the primary purpose of the Statement of Applicability in an ISMS?

options.text: To record which controls apply and justify inclusions and exclusions
options.rationale: Correct: the SoA documents control selection against assessed risk.
The SoA does not contain credentials.
The SoA follows from, not replaces, the risk assessment.

options.text: To guarantee no incidents will occur
options.rationale: No document guarantees the absence of incidents.

items.explanation: Correct: the SoA records applicable controls and justifies inclusions/exclusions.

items.stem: Which TWO activities help sustain an ISMS over time? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: internal audits check the ISMS keeps working.
Correct: review and improvement keep the system current.

options.text: Writing policies once and never revisiting them
options.rationale: Static policies drift out of date and lose value.
Concealing issues undermines improvement and trust.

items.explanation: Correct: internal audits and management review/improvement sustain the ISMS.

items.stem: Why is risk assessment central to control selection in ISO/IEC 27001?

options.text: Controls are chosen to treat assessed risks, not applied arbitrarily
options.rationale: Correct: the standard ties control selection to identified risks.

options.text: Because every control must always be applied in full
options.rationale: Controls are selected based on applicability to risk.

options.text: Because risk assessment replaces the need for controls
options.rationale: Assessment informs, it does not replace, controls.
Risk is explicitly central to the standard.

items.explanation: Correct: controls are selected to treat assessed risks.
